page: Amazon Web Services c8ib.metal-48xl is a bare-metal compute-optimized server powered by dedicated Intel x86_64 processors. The system delivers 96 physical cores and 192 vCPUs running at a clock frequency of 3.9 GHz, supported by two hardware threads per core. System memory totals 384.0 GB of RAM, establishing a compute-oriented allocation of 2.0 GB per vCPU or 4.0 GB per physical core.

The hardware configuration includes no integrated graphical processing units and contains no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage architectures for non-volatile data persistence. Network connectivity features a baseline throughput of 200 Gbps, accommodating high-throughput distributed data exchange, while no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned directly to the host.

From an architectural standpoint, the dedicated physical infrastructure eliminates virtualization overhead and noisy-neighbor interference across high-concurrency tasks. Because memory density is modest relative to core count and local disks are absent, the server optimizes resource allocation toward dense processing pipelines rather than data caching. It fits distributed high-performance computing clusters, intensive batch jobs, scientific modeling, large-scale continuous integration compilation, and compute-focused distributed simulations.
description: Amazon Web Services c8ib.metal-48xl is a bare-metal compute-optimized server engineered for processing-intensive enterprise workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture with dedicated Intel processors, the machine provides 96 physical cores, 192 vCPUs operating at 3.9 GHz, and 384.0 GB of system memory, matching a 2.0 GB per vCPU distribution ratio. The hardware contains zero GPUs and does not supply onboard local storage, necessitating external network block storage for persistence. Network capabilities are defined by a high-throughput 200 Gbps baseline interface without included public IPv4 addresses. Removing hypervisor layers ensures predictable low-latency execution across all dedicated cores. This makes the host suitable for high-performance computing, large batch processing pipelines, parallel compilation jobs, video encoding clusters, and distributed simulation algorithms requiring consistent processor performance without virtualization contention.
